_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_session: SkyLead, Session 221 — the table leads, and the explainer is the public view
_status: The Implementation Funding tab now opens on the introduction (with the Summary inside it) and the institution table right underneath; everything else — the funding window, the breakdown, the formula, the eligibility requirements, the outcomes and the timing — is folded until you open it, and the folds start closed on every visit rather than remembering last time. The priority boxes are all the same width, and the line that restated a priority's window funding is gone because the band heading and the box already carry those numbers. The public explainer, How this funding model works, is now the public view: its Every institution section sits right after the introduction and is the tab's own table — same rows, same click-to-open detail, same search and Excel download — and it now shows the timing milestones and each priority's recommended strategies. The old public page is still live; whether it becomes a redirect to the explainer is Sam's call.

items.text: Confirm the explainer (How this funding model works) as the one public page, and whether the old public page (cpl_funding_public.html) should become a redirect to it so there is a single public link. Then react by letter to this run's calls: (a) the explainer's steps fold closed on open like the tab's sections; (b) its own four-column table is retired in favor of the tab's rows; (c) the table's footnote sits under the table; (d) section folds are no longer remembered across visits; (e) the embedded table sits in the explainer's narrower column, where its toolbar wraps to two lines. Reply keep, edit, or revert per letter.

React to the calm pass's judgment calls on the Implementation Funding tab, by letter: (a) the subtitle under the title is gone; (b) the college's name is what opens its detail, no caret; (c) the sort arrow is the one mark kept, ghosted; (d) the CPL area word stays as muted text by the project picker; (e) a scenario with edits reads (edited) in the picker; (f) the held-in-reserve amount reads inside the eligibility sentence and again ahead of Total Possible; (g) the eligibility introduction is prose with an Edit word for reviewers. Reply keep, edit, or revert per letter.

Say whether more of the tab's text should be editable in place. Five sections are today (the introduction, Reading the funding, the eligibility introduction, the noncredit earning rules, the table introduction). Any other paragraph is one registry entry away.

Set the funding dials on this tab: Accepted at 25% share and factor 1.0, with the starting set Eligible 40% / Accepted 25% / Transcribed 35%. These are yours to save here rather than something a session writes into the database for you. Once they are in, the earning diagnostic is worth re-running — it is what showed that 84% of everything earned came from the one measure almost every college already meets, and it will read differently now.

Decide whether the Annual view should keep showing earning above 100%. An award cell can read "earning $140,476 · 191%" there, because earning is a window quantity measured against a per-year figure. That is deliberate, but two readers have now read it as over-earning. Keep it as is, or compute the percent against the window figure.

Say whether the shareable copy of How this funding model works should be refreshed. Its two illustration figures were computed on the old sizing basis, so one card disagrees with the table beside it. Refreshing is a single command, but it needs the live settings pulled from the database, so it is worth doing deliberately rather than in passing. The public page is already correct.

Once Sam confirms: make cpl_funding_public.html a redirect to funding-model/ (keep the URL alive), repoint the ledger note's public-page link, re-aim the public/private test onto the explainer, and re-label the tab's Internal · Public preview for what it now previews.

Add the explainer to the on-demand layout harness (scripts/check_public_page_layout.js measures Sierra alone today) so its folds, the embedded scrolling table, the tap-target sizes and every contrast pair are measured in a real browser rather than claimed.

One request to Pedro carrying all three feed additions: the CPL lifecycle booleans (sent 2026-09-01), Origin and LocID2, and completions. Completions needs a new MAP view — the existing student view has no award column and the programs view is a catalog. Completion data would let the Completion outcome be measured in the statute's own word.

Repair the explainer's browser check. It waits for an element id retired long ago, and also pins a dollar figure and a college count that have both moved. It fails the same way on main and sits outside the main test run, so nothing has been reporting it.
Cut the dead CSS left behind by the retired row shapes — about fifteen rules for shapes the one-pool model removed, plus a stale selector in the frozen-header code.
